name: Ethiopia economy and return benchmarks
summary: Ethiopia's real GDP grew 9.2 percent in FY2024/25 under an IMF-supported reform program that moved the birr to a market-based exchange rate in July 2024 and introduced an interest-rate-based monetary policy framework. Inflation has fallen from 26.6 percent on average in FY2023/24 but rose again to 13.4 percent in May 2026, and the National Bank of Ethiopia raised its policy rate by 1 percentage point in July 2026. FDI reached a reported USD 4.32 billion in FY2025/26, while public debt is still assessed as in distress pending completion of the restructuring.

indicators.label: Real GDP growth
indicators.value: 9.2 percent (FY2024/25); IMF projects 7.8 percent for FY2025/26 and 8.2 percent for FY2026/27

indicators.label: Headline inflation (year-on-year)
indicators.value: 13.4 percent (food 15.0 percent, non-food 11.1 percent), up from 11.7 percent in April 2026 and 9.7 percent in December 2025

indicators.label: Average inflation (IMF)
indicators.value: 26.6 percent (FY2023/24), 16.0 percent (FY2024/25), 11.7 percent (FY2025/26 est.), 12.3 percent (FY2026/27 proj.)

indicators.label: Exchange rate regime and level
indicators.value: Market-based exchange rate system since July 29, 2024; weighted average rate at the May 19, 2026 NBE FX auction 159.63 ETB per USD; parallel market spread 10-20 percent since October 2025, about 11 percent in late May 2026

indicators.label: Foreign direct investment inflows
indicators.value: USD 4.32 billion, up 8 percent from the previous year (EIC figures)

indicators.label: Gross reserves
indicators.value: 2.1 months of imports (FY2025/26), projected 2.7 months (FY2026/27), up from 0.7 months in FY2023/24

indicators.label: Debt and credit standing (IMF assessment)
indicators.value: Debt 'continues to be assessed as unsustainable and in distress'; restructuring aims to improve the rating to moderate risk by end of program; agreement-in-principle reached with Eurobond holders

returns.label: NBE policy rate (National Bank Rate)
returns.period: As displayed on NBE homepage, accessed 2026-10-16
returns.basis: Central bank policy rate; standing facilities at NBR plus or minus 3 percentage points

returns.label: Policy rate decision
returns.value: Raised by 1.0 percentage point (from the initial 15 percent set in July 2024 and held through March 2026)
returns.basis: MPC decision; prior level of 15 percent per NBE framework announcement and IMF staff report

returns.label: Treasury bill weighted average yield, all tenors
returns.value: 12.3 percent (down from 15.5 percent a year earlier)
returns.basis: Weighted average yield on all Treasury bills

returns.label: 91-day Treasury bill yield
returns.value: 11.0 percent (down from 16.1 percent a year earlier)

returns.label: Treasury bill yield on new issuance (IMF)
returns.value: 14.4 percent, down from 16.7 percent in December 2025
returns.basis: Weighted average rate on new T-bill issuances

returns.label: Interbank rate (7-day)
returns.value: 14.6 percent, down from about 18.0 percent in March 2026

returns.label: Commercial bank long-term lending rate
returns.basis: Weighted average long-term lending interest rate of commercial banks

returns.label: Average lending and deposit rates
returns.value: Average lending rate 15.0 percent (range 7.0-23.0 percent); weighted average time deposit rate 7.8 percent; average savings rate 8.0 percent
returns.basis: Interest rate structure of the banking system, NBE Table 4.4

returnsNote: Benchmark yields and rates above are published by the National Bank of Ethiopia and the IMF; NBE liberalized deposit and lending rates in January 2026 (no floors or caps), so the Q1 FY2024/25 average lending and deposit rates are the latest full interest-rate structure we found.

opportunities.title: Energy, health, transport and logistics
opportunities.detail: Listed by EIC as other sectors of opportunity: electricity for a large unserved population, an underserved healthcare sector, and logistics for a landlocked country.

incentives.detail: Investors establishing a new enterprise are entitled to an income tax exemption, with length depending on sub-sector, export volume and location; losses during the exemption period can be carried forward.
Duty-free import of capital goods and construction materials for new or expanding enterprises.

Capital repatriation and remittance of dividends and interest are guaranteed to foreign investors under the Investment Proclamation; minimum foreign investment capital is USD 200,000 (USD 150,000 in a joint venture with a domestic investor).
FX liberalization continued in July 2026: the FX commission was reduced from 2.5 to 1.5 percent and the export surrender requirement on goods from 50 to 30 percent.

risks.detail: Inflation rebounded to 13.4 percent in May 2026 from 9.7 percent in December 2025, prompting a 1 percentage point policy rate increase; the IMF says NBE should be ready to tighten further.
Public debt remains assessed by the IMF as unsustainable and in distress until the restructuring is complete; some Eurobond holders' committee members indicated they intend to pursue legal action.
The parallel market exchange rate spread has fluctuated between 10 and 20 percent since October 2025, and the birr depreciated about 1.3 percent per month.
The IMF brought forward about USD 200 million to address pressures from the war in the Middle East, especially higher fuel import costs.
